title: 3 nodes with nvidia.com/gpu have no utilisation source
evidence: Node/ip-10-0-1-11.us-west-2.compute.internal: 4 × nvidia.com/gpu (g5.12xlarge), no metrics source runs on it
Node/ip-10-0-1-12.us-west-2.compute.internal: 4 × nvidia.com/gpu (g5.12xlarge), no metrics source runs on it
Node/ip-10-0-1-13.us-west-2.compute.internal: 4 × nvidia.com/gpu (g5.12xlarge), no metrics source runs on it

fix.summary: Install NVIDIA's dcgm-exporter chart as the stack's NVIDIA metrics source (forge.Install, pinned); forge scrapes it with the allow list in ml.k.

title: 2 Jobs request accelerators with no queue: no fair share or preemption

fix.summary: Install Kueue as the stack's queue (forge.Install, pinned; delivery "bootstrap" because it ships CRDs, so apply it with `forge env deploy <env> --target kueue`), then give each team a LocalQueue and label jobs with kueue.x-k8s.io/queue-name. The diff also installs JobSet (`--target jobset`), Kueue's unit for multi-pod training.

title: 3 accelerator nodes have no node health detection: bad nodes keep getting work
evidence: no node-problem-detector, no EKS node monitoring agent, and no node condition a health source sets

fix.summary: First option: the EKS node monitoring agent add-on with node auto repair, which sets AcceleratedHardwareReady and replaces bad GPU nodes. Otherwise install node-problem-detector as the stack's node_health, with a kernel-log rule that sets GPUProblem on a fatal NVIDIA Xid.

title: Accelerator images fan out to many nodes with no peer-to-peer pull cache

fix.summary: Install Spegel as the stack's pull_cache (one small DaemonSet: nodes pull layers from each other instead of the registry). It needs containerd's registry config_path and discard_unpacked_layers=false; check its compatibility notes for your node image first.

title: 2 workloads run accelerators with the 64 MiB /dev/shm default
evidence: Job/ml/hparam-sweep: 4 pods, container trial mounts no memory emptyDir at /dev/shm
Job/ml/train-llama-ft: 1 pod, container train mounts no memory emptyDir at /dev/shm

fix.summary: Mount an emptyDir {medium: Memory} (with a sizeLimit) at /dev/shm in each accelerator container: NCCL, PyTorch DataLoader workers and vLLM's tensor parallelism need more than 64 MiB.

title: 3 spot accelerator nodes get no graceful interruption notice

fix.summary: Install aws-node-termination-handler in queue mode (its helm chart, oci://public.ecr.aws/aws-ec2/helm/aws-node-termination-handler), or, if Karpenter provisions these nodes, set its interruption queue (settings.interruptionQueue), so a two-minute notice drains pods and lets training checkpoint.

title: 1 accelerator image is over 10 GB: weights are likely baked into the image
evidence: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/train:2026-11-18: 14.1 GB on Node/ip-10-0-1-11.us-west-2.compute.internal, used by Job/ml/hparam-sweep, Job/ml/train-llama-ft

fix.summary: Split it into a weights artifact (a CNCF ModelPack OCI artifact, one layer per weight file) and a slim runtime image, so a code change does not re-pull the weights.

title: 1 node had idle, unrequested accelerators at snapshot time
evidence: pool gpu-spot: Node/ip-10-0-1-13.us-west-2.compute.internal: 4 × nvidia.com/gpu allocatable, none requested

fix.summary: One snapshot is not a trend. If these nodes stay unrequested, lower the pool's minimum size in its autoscaler (cluster autoscaler, Karpenter, the cloud's node pool) so it scales down.

title: 1 container downloads from Hugging Face without the fast path
evidence: Job/ml/train-llama-ft: train downloads hf://meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B from the Hugging Face Hub with neither HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE nor HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER set

fix.summary: Set HF_XET_HIGH_PERFORMANCE=1 (huggingface_hub with hf_xet; HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER is deprecated), or better, stop downloading per pod.

title: 1 accelerator image is not warm on every node of its pool
evidence: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/train:2026-11-18: not on ip-10-0-1-13.us-west-2.compute.internal (pool gpu-spot; present on 2 of 3 nodes)
node.status.images lists at most 50 images per node by default, so a busy node may hold an image it does not list

fix.summary: Pre-pull the image on the pool (a pre-pull DaemonSet, kube-fledged), or bake it into the node image (GKE: a secondary boot disk), so a new pod does not wait for the pull.

title: No continuous profiling on the accelerator nodes

fix.summary: Run one continuous eBPF profiler as a DaemonSet on the accelerator nodes: Parca agent, Grafana Alloy with pyroscope.ebpf, or the OpenTelemetry eBPF profiler (otel/opentelemetry-collector-ebpf-profiler). It shows where CPU time goes in data loaders and serving code with no code change.
Install an OpenTelemetry Collector with an otlp receiver (grpc :4317, http :4318) so vLLM, Triton and training jobs can export traces and metrics.

title: Image volumes are unavailable: weights cannot be mounted from an OCI artifact without a sidecar
evidence: API server v1.30.8-eks-2d98532: the ImageVolume feature gate is on by default from Kubernetes 1.35

fix.summary: Upgrade to Kubernetes 1.35+ with containerd 2.1+ to mount weights as an image volume. Until then, KServe's modelcar sidecar or an init-container copy is the fallback.

title: 2 accelerator Jobs export no OTLP traces

fix.summary: Set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME) on the Job's containers, or inject an SDK with an OpenTelemetry Instrumentation resource, so steps and data-loading spans reach your collector.
